AH3-02.solved: Synthetic division by (x-3) on 1,-6,-1,30 gives 1,-3,-10 remainder 0, so p(x)=(x-3)(x^2-3x-10)=(x-3)(x-5)(x+2). Other zeros 5 and -2; greatest is 5.
AH3-02.note: -2 is the genuine other zero; -10 is the product of the other two roots and 10 its sign flip. One routine idea (divide, factor), not a two-idea item.

AH3-04.solved: Half-hour factor is 1.44^(1/2)=1.2, so a 20% increase per half hour.
AH3-04.note: Borderline hard - the rate-over-a-different-interval move is the one place in this batch a weak student is genuinely stranded. 72 (half of 44) and 44 (the hourly rate) are both real student paths; 120 is the multiplier misread as a percent.

AH3-05.solved: Square: 3x+22 = x^2+8x+16 -> x^2+5x-6=0 -> (x+6)(x-1)=0 -> x=1 or x=-6. x=-6 gives RHS=-2<0, extraneous. Check x=1: sqrt(25)=5=1+4.
AH3-05.note: The extraneous-root check is the whole item and -6 is sitting right there, which is correct design. Stem says 'the solution' (singular), consistent with exactly one surviving root - no ambiguity.

AH3-06.solved: 3x^2-11x-4 = (3x+1)(x-4), so f(x)=3x+1 for x!=4. Continuity forces g(4)=3(4)+1=13.
AH3-06.note: 12 (dropping the +1), 0 (assuming a hole means zero) and -1/3 (the root of the surviving factor) are all real wrong paths.

AH3-07.solved: f min -5 at x=2. g(x)=f(x+3)-4 needs x+3=2 -> x=-1, and the value drops by 4 to -9. Minimum at (-1,-9).
AH3-07.note: Clean 2x2 option grid: shift direction crossed with vertical shift. No narrowing possible from the options alone.

AH3-08.note: Plainly an easy item - one substitution after -b/2a. 79 is f(-3) and 3 is the x-coordinate; 16 is loose. This would not appear on the module-2 hard route.

AH3-09.note: 3 is the other (greatest) root, which is the right trap for 'least'. -3 and 4 cover the sign-flip slips.

AH3-11.solved: x^2+10x+c = 6x+5 -> x^2+4x+(c-5)=0. One intersection means discriminant 0: 16-4(c-5)=0 -> c-5=4 -> c=9.
AH3-11.note: 25 = (10/2)^2, a student who completes the square before subtracting the line. -2 and -1 are weaker; I cannot name a clean path to -1.

AH3-12.solved: Multiply through by (x-2)(x+2): x+8 = 3(x+2) = 3x+6 -> 2x = 2 -> x = 1. x=1 is in the domain.
AH3-12.note: 7 comes from cross-multiplying to 3(x-2) (forgetting the difference of squares) and 2 is an excluded value - both are exactly what students produce.

AH3-13.note: 5 is the answer if the remainder is taken as 0 (the far more common textbook version); 27 is 3k left unsolved. Good set.

AH3-14.solved: Let u=x^2: u^2-13u+36=0 -> u=4 or 9 -> x = +-2, +-3. Positive solutions 2 and 3, sum 5.
AH3-14.note: 6 is the product of the positive solutions, 0 the sum of all four, 9 one of the u-values.

AH3-15.note: 2x2 grid again (stretch direction x output scaling). Note the batch carries two horizontal-transformation items, AH3-07 and this one, testing nearly the same reflex.

AH3-18.note: Easy. The three distractors are the sign permutations, which is systematic but low-effort; a student who factors correctly cannot land on any of them. Domain restrictions in the stem (x!=3, x!=-2) agree with the factorisation.

AH3-19.note: One substitution; the vertex is handed to the student in the given form, so nothing has to be derived. Easy. 12 is 4a unsolved, 1/3 the reciprocal.

AH3-20.note: Two log rules applied once each, no interaction. 21 = 15+6 (sign slip) is the only distractor with a real path; 2.5 and 6 are weak.

AH3-21.note: Mild options-only narrowing: 81 is the only perfect fourth power in the set, so a student who knows only that x must be a fourth power of an integer can pick it without doing the exponent arithmetic. Not decisive, but worth noting. 9 = 27^(2/3) is the real trap.

AH3-22.note: The one genuinely hard item in the batch: factored form and vertex form have to interact - find a from the intercepts plus a point, then convert to get k. Distractors 2 and 3 are exactly a and h, which is the correct trap for students who stop one step early. 32 catches the sign.

AH3-23.note: 400 (dropping the +1), 403 (adding 3 instead of multiplying) and 120 (doubling rather than squaring) are all live paths.

AH3-24.note: Leans easy - the identity is one line and needs no solving for x and y. 4 comes from subtracting instead of adding 2xy, 8 is x+y left unsquared.
